extracted.intended_audience: plain TeX users, macro writers, and typesetters (macro designers and advanced TeX users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, conventions, and implementation notes for writing and debugging plain TeX macros and documents (appendix material from The TeXbook). Covers control-sequence conventions, layout/box/leader/table techniques, output routines, spacing and glue behavior, and numeric/resource limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \nointerlineskip with \moveright
rubrics_metrics.description: The interline skip is added for vboxes but not for rules; you must say \nointerlineskip before and after the \moveright construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you omit \nointerlineskip before/after a \moveright, extra interline glue may be inserted where it's not wanted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \vrule in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: When producing a rule that appears in horizontal mode, it is necessary to call it a \vrule since it appeared in horizontal mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \vrule height3pt depth-2pt width1in; calling it properly avoids mode-related errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box macros affect baseline — adjust baseline explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: A boxed construction (e.g., \vbox inside a wrapper macro) does not automatically preserve the baseline of the original box; you must work to get the baseline right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example \def\boxit#1{\vbox{\hrule\hbox{\vrule\kern3pt \vbox{\kern3pt#1\kern3pt}\kern3pt\vrule}\hrule}} demonstrates a boxed macro whose baseline differs; additional spacing or alignment is required to restore original baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand differences among leaders, \cleaders, \xleaders
rubrics_metrics.description: leaders, \cleaders, \xleaders differ in how sequences of boxes begin and repeat (e.g., two boxes starting at 100pt vs three starting at other offsets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate leader type depending on intended alignment: leaders start at the left, \cleaders center a repeating pattern across the available space, \xleaders distribute to align at regular offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define custom leader fill macros carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: You can define a leader-fill macro (example given in text) to produce dotted or patterned fills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: \def\leaderfill{\kern-0.3em\leaders\hbox to 1em{\hss.\hss}%\hskip0.6em plus\fill \kern-0.3em } — shows precise spacing tweaks necessary for visual effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always specify height/depth for \vrule when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If no height or depth specification follows a \vrule, the height and depth are set to the smallest enclosing box, which often makes a heavy black band.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting explicit height/depth can produce undesirable thick black bands; specify dimensions or use \leaders\vrule\vfill in vertical mode where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent leaders disappearing at page tops: use \null and \nobreak
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep leaders from disappearing at a page break, prefix with \null\nobreak before \leaders... and choose fill glue appropriately (fill vs \parfillskip).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Example: 
ull
obreak\leaders\hrule\hskip10pt plus ill \par — 
ull preserves glue, 
obreak prevents break at that point, and the chosen glue overtakes \parfillskip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defer expansion when writing to files (use \let\the=0 trick)
rubrics_metrics.description: To expand everything but the \the used by \write, temporarily set \let\the=0 and build an \edef that contains a \write; this defers \the until the write actually executes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: {\let\the=0 \edef\next{\write\cont{(token list)}}\next} — useful for controlling when tokens are expanded for output files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \smallskip to separate table heading/footing from table
rubrics_metrics.description: Small vertical skips (\smallskip) are often worthwhile to separate the table heading and footing from the table itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refinements like \smallskip improve table appearance compared to cramming headings directly against table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reset tabs with \cleartabs before a leading & and set multiletter identifiers in \it
rubrics_metrics.description: In tabbing/tabular programs it's best to type \cleartabs just before &1 whenever it is desirable to reset the old tabs. Multiletter identifiers look best when set in text italics with \it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example style recommendation: use \+\bf While $p>0$ do\cr and in subsequent lines mark control sequences appropriately; the preamble should reflect desired indentation and font choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \halign/\valign family for general alignments; define preamble macros when repeated
rubrics_metrics.description: General alignments use \halign, \valign, \omit, \span, \multispan; if a preamble pattern repeats, define a macro (e.g., \def\Welshverb#1{...}) for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defining a preamble macro simplifies complicated alignment specifications and avoids duplication (example given for Welsh verb table).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle italic slant and kerning in table title lines (repeat font switches per column)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title line may need repeated font declarations because each entry between tabs is treated as a group; small backspaces such as \negthinspace may compensate for italic slant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title line might specify \it three times in preamble; manual tweaks (\negthinspace) can improve look of italic characters like 'l'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase \tolerance for narrow measures/long words
rubrics_metrics.description: With narrow measure and long words you may need to increase \tolerance (e.g., to 1000) inside a \vtop to avoid overfull or excessive hyphenation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusting \tolerance locally is preferable to relaxing layout globally; try the smallest increase that fixes line-breaking problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center multi-part displayed equations with \halign using tabskip glue
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the equation into parts for terms and plus/minus signs and use tabskip glue in a \halign to center them across the display width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example layout shows multiple alignment columns with explicit tabskip settings and use of \openup\jot to control interline spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \multispan, \dotfill, \bigstrut etc. to improve table aesthetics
rubrics_metrics.description: To add extra vertical space around titles or to make rules/spacing align, include \omit lines with height2pt, use \multispan with \hrulefill, or place \bigstrut boxes in title columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either technique makes the table look better; choose depending on whether you want an invisible box or an explicit rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place empty columns at table extremes to allow \hrulefill to span tabskip glue
rubrics_metrics.description: Having 'empty' columns at the extreme left and right enables \hrulefill (or \hrulefill-like constructs) to span the available tabskip glue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the preamble so outer columns are blank, enabling rule fills to stretch across the desired region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \valign to transpose rows and columns when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: \valign transposes rows and columns of a vertical alignment construction, which can be used to solve puzzles or construct certain grid layouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: placing vertical lists into a \valign converted the intended pennies-grid into the required arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set page headers/footers with \headline and \footline; use \nopagenumbers and adjust \voffset
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \headline and \footline to control page headings and footers. Also say \nopagenumbers and adjust \voffset to shift output vertically when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \footline={\tenrm-- \folio --\tenrm} and \headline conditional on \pageno illustrate customizing first page vs others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write custom \output routines to build multi-column or specialized page formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign \output to a macro (or chain of macros) that captures columns into boxes and then \shipout a composed page (e.g., triple-column format using \box\leftcolumn, \box\midcolumn, \columnbox).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical pattern: gather column boxes into global boxes with flags L/M/R, then on \output assemble and \shipout a vbox containing headline, composed columns, and footline; remember to \advancepageno and handle \superejects at end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid breakpoints between \mark and \leftline: use \nobreak or place marks after boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Interline glue is inserted automatically before \leftline, permitting a legal breakpoint between a \mark and the \leftline box; remedy by saying \nobreak just after the \mark or by placing marks/insertions after boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing marks and insertions right after boxes avoids undesirable splits; \nobreak is a localized fix but preferred placement is after boxed material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer \ifcase approach (with \expandafter\relax\botmark) for efficient parsing of \botmark components
rubrics_metrics.description: To read parts of the \botmark, e.g. component 2, use \ifcase2\expandafter\relax\botmark\fi; the \ifcase method lets TeX pass over unselected components at high speed and is usually more efficient than alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, put components into macro parameters, but that can be less efficient than \ifcase when skipping parts is common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make \vsize large enough to hold index continuation lines (avoid infinite looping)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the text of main and subsidiary index entries is lengthy, continuation lines may occur inside the \output routine; \vsize must be large enough to accommodate all continuation lines plus at least one more line of index material, otherwise infinite looping can occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure page body size is sufficient for the index format or redesign the index output routine to handle continuations safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of \meaning behavior for \chardef and \mathchardef
rubrics_metrics.description: If a control sequence has been defined by \chardef or \mathchardef, TeX uses hexadecimal notation when it expands \meaning\cs and assigns category 12 to each digit of the expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subtlety can affect parsing or further expansion if you rely on \meaning output; it is mainly relevant in obscure applications where you treat parts of \meaning as numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace rules: any number of spaces may precede a keyword
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX permits any number of spaces before any keyword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general parsing behavior that allows flexible input spacing; do not rely on significant leading spaces for control flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glue and token-coercion subtleties (final space swallowed, integer->dimen coercion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an internal integer appears as an (internal unit) in glue/dimen contexts it is coerced to a dimension; final spaces can be swallowed as part of optional spaces in the (shrink) part of syntax for glue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that presence/absence of PLUS/MINUS parts affects whether following spaces become part of glue; this influences computed stretch/shrink and visual spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \everyjob to set up batch/dump-time input (example for \dump)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can set \everyjob to run commands at format/dump time; example given: \everyjob={\batchmode\input\jobname\end} to prepare a batch run that inputs the job file and ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when creating dumped formats or automating batch processing; test carefully to avoid accidental infinite loops or unintended input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debugging `Missing number' errors: guard macros and use \tracingcommands=1
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords like plus, minus, width, depth, or height can appear in text while TeX expects a number in a glue or rule specification; general-purpose macros should guard against this. If you get a 'Missing number' error, insert \tracingcommands=1 shortly before the error to see what TeX is doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice defensive macro writing (e.g., end a macro with \relax where appropriate) and use \tracingcommands to inspect the log to track why TeX is expecting a number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know TeX's numeric and resource limits and badness/penalty semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Radix-10 notation is used for numeric constants and output. Badness values: a box whose glue has stretched/shrunk to stated stretchability/shrinkability has badness 100; badness is at most 10000 (overfull box has 1000000 in INITEX?). Penalty thresholds: penalties >=10000 prohibit breaks, penalties <= -10000 make breaks mandatory. INITEX initializes \tolerance to 10000, making all line breaks feasible. Page-break cost conventions (e.g., cost 100000 when badness 10000 and penalties less than 10000) are described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand these thresholds when tuning \tolerance, penalties, and designing breaking-sensitive macros or layouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX table sizes and code limits (register counts, font size, dimen limits, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 256 possible characters and 256 entries in each of the \catcode, \mathcode, \lccode, \uccode, \sfcode, and \delcode tables. A font has at most 256 characters. The 'at' size of a font must be less than 2048pt. A dimen value's magnitude must be less than 16384pt. Various code and value ranges (for \mathchar, \spacefactor, \delcode, etc.) have upper bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing macros or allocating registers, be aware of these implementation limits; many numbers are implementation-dependent, but the book lists typical hard limits to avoid overflow or undefined behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of reserved/special characters and primary control sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX reserves characters for special purposes: \  {  }  $  &  #  %  _  ^  ~  etc. and provides line-break controls (\break, \nobreak, \allowbreak), breakable/unbreakable space commands (~, \enskip, \quad, \hskip), vertical spaces (\smallskip, \medskip, \bigskip), and page break controls (\eject, \supereject, \nobreak).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the summary chart and use the appropriate primitives for spacing and breaking; these are the building blocks of higher-level plain.tex macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not edit plain.tex; extend formats by loading plain.fmt or using format mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX's format file (plain.tex) should not be modified under ordinary circumstances; if you want a new format that adds features, it is better to load plain.fmt and extend it (e.g., via \input of a supplement or use the format-dumping mechanism) rather than copying/modifying the whole plain.tex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you must modify, change the version number when you do so and prefer to create separate format (e.g., 'plain super') rather than duplicating the entire format file to avoid maintenance problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: When solving problems, try yourself first but use answers as last resort
rubrics_metrics.description: If you can't solve a problem, you can look up the answer, but please try first to solve it by yourself; then you'll learn more and learn faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical advice for learners working through TeX exercises; encourages independent problem solving before consulting solutions.
